questions.stem: A pmf has P(X = 1) = 1/2, P(X = 2) = 1/3 and P(X = 3) = p. What is p?
questions.explain: The probabilities add to 1. 1/2 + 1/3 = 5/6, so p = 1 − 5/6 = 1/6.

questions.stem: A pmf is P(X = k) = c·k for k = 1, 2, 3, 4. What is c?
questions.explain: The probabilities must add to 1: c(1 + 2 + 3 + 4) = 10c = 1, so c = 0.1.

questions.stem: A coin is tossed 3 times. In how many of the 8 outcomes are there exactly 2 heads?
questions.explain: Choose which 2 of the 3 tosses are heads: C(3, 2) = 3 (HHT, HTH, THH).

questions.stem: The function g(x) = x² is applied to the values −2, −1, 0, 1, 2. How many different outputs appear?
questions.explain: The outputs are 4, 1, 0, 1, 4, which contain only 3 different values. Different inputs can share one output.

questions.stem: Which list of numbers can be the probabilities of three outcomes?
questions.explain: Probabilities cannot be negative and must add to exactly 1. Only 0.5 + 0.3 + 0.2 = 1 with all values at least 0.
